name: Plastic/silicone tools
anchor: EU food-contact framework Regulation 1935/2004 with Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II specific migration limits as the only element-migration instrument in the register expressed in the food-contact FOOD basis (the register's other migration instruments — the EU 2009/48 toy Categories I to III and the ASTM F963 soluble limits — are in the toy article-extraction basis and are barred from every row of this category). Rows whose principal food-contact surface is a polymer anchor it directly, or by disclosed read-across where the instrument's own scope article excludes or does not reach the material or where the taxonomy row also carries a non-plastic configuration. Metal, alloy, ceramic-glaze, vitreous-enamel and glass rows, and the two water-treatment-device rows, are controls because their dedicated release regimes (Directive 84/500/EEC as amended by 2005/31/EC, the metals-and-alloys release regime, and the drinking-water device route) are not in the register in their own jurisdictions' rows. Where one taxonomy row carries both a polymer and a metal configuration, the published cells take the metal-article control and the plastics value is disclosed as a film-only companion.
native_basis: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food), Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II convention
native_basis_label: specific element migration INTO FOOD OR A FOOD SIMULANT from the polymeric food-contact surface, µg/kg of food, determined by the Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex III to V simulant, temperature and contact-time conventions. This is a MIGRATION basis and not a total-content basis: no cell on this row limits how much of an element the material CONTAINS, and no cell on this row is expressed per kg of material.
scope_note: Hand tools whose food-contact head is a polymer. Plastic heads are articles consisting exclusively of plastics and are directly within Reg (EU) 10/2011; SILICONE heads are excluded from that instrument by its Art. 2(2)(c) and take the identical ceilings by disclosed read-across, which changes no published number. The distinguishing contact condition is short, repeated, HIGH-TEMPERATURE contact against a hot pan surface, well above the ambient migration convention, so the release test must be run at the tool's stated maximum service temperature and after the declared thermal cycling. Bonded metal cores are metal components under the alloy-release regime. Because that read-across is a real provenance difference rather than a wording nuance, every published cell on this row now carries READ-ACROSS provenance rather than regulatory-alignment, and each cell's label and substantiation name which configuration the instrument governs directly and which takes the value by read-across. No published number changes.
material: Nylon, polypropylene and melamine-composite turners, spoons and ladles; silicone spatulas, brushes and whisks, frequently with a bonded stainless or plastic core; thermoplastic-elastomer overmoulded grips; pigmented and printed tool heads.
components: Sample and report separately: (1) polymer tool head at its stated maximum service temperature, third successive migration governing; (2) silicone heads as their own lot, under the disclosed read-across; (3) bonded stainless or metal core, tested where it is exposed at a worn edge, under the alloy-release regime; (4) overmoulded grip where it can reach food or the user's mouth; (5) pigment masterbatch verification for lead chromate, cadmium pigment and chrome green; (6) tool head after the declared thermal-cycling and dishwasher conditioning.
basis_guard_note: Only an instrument expressed as specific element migration into food or a food simulant may anchor a cell on this row. The guard exists to reject the three foreign bases that surround this category and would otherwise look plausible: the FOOD basis (canned-food tin maximum levels, which limit the contents and not the article), the MATERIAL-CONTENT basis (CPSIA total lead in substrate, EU REACH Annex XVII cadmium percent-by-weight restrictions, RoHS homogeneous-material limits, Japan Notice 370 and Korea MFDS percent-by-weight lead in food-contact metals), and the ARTICLE-EXTRACTION basis of the toy regime (EU 2009/48 Annex II Part III and ASTM F963 soluble limits, which are element migration from scraped-off or coated TOY material into 0.07 M hydrochloric acid, expressed per kg of MATERIAL, not per kg of food). Any of those would fail this guard and resolve to a gap rather than publish in the wrong basis.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only): the strictest applicable sovereign maximum for this exact product form expressed as specific element migration into food or a food simulant; a disclosed read-across from the nearest applicable sovereign value in the same basis where the food-contact material family is expressly excluded from or not reached by that instrument; a substantiated not-material determination; or a control. No cell is occurrence-derived, and no cell borrows a value across a basis.

Pb.basis: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
Pb.label: read-across on the identical basis of the Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2: lead not detectable in the food or simulant, detection limit 0.01 mg/kg food
Pb.substantiation: Lead is on the Annex II point 2 not-detectable list, so the published ceiling is the 0.01 mg/kg food detection limit and not a positive migration allowance. Plastic tool heads are within this instrument's direct scope; silicone heads are excluded by Art. 2(2)(c) and take the same values by disclosed read-across. This is a migration ceiling on the food or simulant and is never reported as a limit on the material's lead content; the material-content instruments (US CPSIA total lead in children's-product substrate, Japan Notice 370 and Korea MFDS 2024-29 percent-by-weight lead in food-contact metals and solder) are separate obligations in a different basis and are not this cell. PROVENANCE NOTE: this cell is tagged READ-ACROSS rather than regulatory-alignment because this taxonomy row covers two material configurations. The plastic tool head, an article consisting exclusively of plastics is within the instrument's direct scope, and for that configuration the value is a direct sovereign maximum. The silicone tool head is expressly excluded from the instrument by its Art. 2(2)(c), with no EU specific measure adopted for silicones, so for that configuration the exact cell is unregulated and the identical value is applied as a DISCLOSED READ-ACROSS holding the basis constant: the same measured quantity, specific element migration into food or a food simulant in ug/kg of food, determined by the same test conventions. The published number is the same for both configurations, so nothing is loosened. The conservative tag is used so that the machine-readable provenance never asserts regulatory alignment to an instrument whose own scope article does not reach one of this row's materials; splitting the row in two, each with its own provenance, is recorded as a taxonomy change for governance.

Cr.basis: specific element migration into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
Cr.label: read-across on the identical basis of the Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II point 2: total chromium not detectable in the food or simulant, detection limit 0.01 mg/kg food; the 3.6 mg/kg food relaxation available on documented exclusion of chromium(VI) is declined
Cr.substantiation: This total-chromium cell is deliberately published as a firm ceiling rather than the usual non-protective total-chromium screen, and the reason is structural to the instrument. Annex II point 2 as amended by Reg (EU) 2020/1245 sets total chromium at not detectable and permits a relaxed 3.6 mg/kg food limit only where the operator documents that chromium(VI) is absent. The non-detect branch therefore exists precisely because hexavalent chromium cannot be assumed absent, which makes it the hexavalent-chromium-conservative form of the requirement rather than a chromium(III)-dominated artefact. HMTc publishes the non-detect branch and declines the relaxation, and the hexavalent-chromium cell is bounded by this value. Plastic tool heads are within this instrument's direct scope; silicone heads are excluded by Art. 2(2)(c) and take the same values by disclosed read-across.
